## Who Is Counted in the Unemployment Rate?

The unemployment rate’s denominator is the labor force: people who are employed plus people classified as unemployed. It does not include everyone who is out of work or considering a job.

Classification depends on the circumstances. Someone on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled can qualify as unemployed without actively searching for work, provided the other criteria are met. By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings has not met the active-search criterion through that activity alone.

Availability for work and the relevant survey reference periods also matter. Being out of work—or looking at listings—does not by itself determine whether someone is counted as unemployed. Those classified as unemployed are included in the labor-force denominator alongside employed people.
